title: SWYRA Auth Canonical Machine-Readable Integration Policy

goldenRules.name: NO_DUPLICATE_AUTH_SYSTEM
goldenRules.statement: NEVER create another authentication system when the centralized IdP is already configured.

goldenRules.name: NO_DIRECT_MONGO_ACCESS
goldenRules.statement: NEVER connect a consumer directly to the IdP's MongoDB for normal authentication.

goldenRules.name: NO_TABLE_COPYING
goldenRules.statement: NEVER copy password/session/token tables from the IdP.

goldenRules.name: NO_BROWSER_CLIENT_SECRET
goldenRules.statement: NEVER expose CLIENT_SECRET to browser code.

goldenRules.name: NO_PUBLIC_CONFIDENTIAL_SECRETS
goldenRules.statement: NEVER put confidential secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC_*, VITE_*, localStorage, sessionStorage, or frontend source.

goldenRules.name: NO_LOCALHOST_PRODUCTION_FALLBACK
goldenRules.statement: NEVER create a localhost production fallback.

goldenRules.name: NO_RUNTIME_CLIENT_CONFLATION
goldenRules.statement: NEVER treat NODE_ENV=production as 'all OAuth clients are production'.

goldenRules.name: NO_AUTHN_AUTHZ_CONFLATION
goldenRules.statement: NEVER treat authentication as application authorization.

goldenRules.name: NO_PROTOCOL_VALIDATION_BYPASS
goldenRules.statement: NEVER bypass the IdP's redirect URI / PKCE / state validation.

public.description: Executed in untrusted client environments (SPAs, mobile apps, desktop native apps) where credentials cannot be kept confidential.

confidential.description: Executed in secure server-side environments (Next.js server, Express, FastAPI, Django, backend services) capable of protecting secrets.

public.description: Open platform access mode. Any registered user in the identity provider pool can sign in. Application membership is automatically recorded upon first login.

private.description: Strict multi-tenant isolation mode. Self-registration is strictly blocked (403 registration_disabled). Only users explicitly provisioned or assigned via the Admin API (POST /api/admin/clients/:clientId/users) may authenticate.

supportedStrategies.name: centralized_oauth2_code_pkce_with_tenant_assignment
supportedStrategies.description: Standard OAuth 2.1 code flow with PKCE redirecting to IdP. If unauthenticated, user is challenged at IdP login page. Assigned users succeed; unassigned users fail with 403 access_denied.

supportedStrategies.name: in_app_credential_relay_app_admin
supportedStrategies.description: Consumer app renders its own custom login page and relays credentials server-to-server via POST /api/auth/app-admin/login. Requires confidential client holding client_secret.

credentialRules.failClosedPolicy: Missing sensitive configuration must throw an unrecoverable startup error or fail closed. Silent fallbacks to localhost or placeholder secrets are strictly prohibited.

forbiddenPatterns.name: IDP_DIRECT_MONGO_ACCESS
forbiddenPatterns.description: Connecting consumer applications directly to IdP MongoDB or referencing MONGO_URI.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Interact exclusively via standard OAuth 2.1 / OIDC HTTP endpoints.

forbiddenPatterns.name: DUPLICATE_AUTH_ENGINE
forbiddenPatterns.description: Installing duplicate auth engines (Better Auth, NextAuth, Auth.js, Passport, Supabase, Lucia) in consumer applications.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Use lightweight OAuth client or JWT verification libraries (jose, pyjwt).

forbiddenPatterns.name: EXPOSED_CLIENT_SECRET
forbiddenPatterns.description: Exposing CLIENT_SECRET to client-side bundles (NEXT_PUBLIC_*, VITE_*, localStorage).
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Confidential clients hold secrets server-side only; public clients use PKCE with no secret.

forbiddenPatterns.name: LOCALHOST_PRODUCTION_FALLBACK
forbiddenPatterns.description: Writing fallback expressions like AUTH_CALLBACK_URL || 'http://localhost:3000/callback' or CLIENT_ID || 'dev-client'.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Configuration must fail closed: throw an explicit error on missing environment variables.

forbiddenPatterns.name: AUTH_PATH_MISDIRECTION
forbiddenPatterns.description: Redirecting authorization requests to the internal SPA path '/auth' instead of '/api/auth/oauth2/authorize'.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Always use the protocol authorization endpoint '/api/auth/oauth2/authorize'.

forbiddenPatterns.name: OMITTED_PKCE_OR_STATE
forbiddenPatterns.description: Skipping PKCE (code_challenge / code_verifier) or state parameter in authorization requests.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Generate S256 PKCE challenge and cryptographically random state for every flow.

forbiddenPatterns.name: ALGORITHM_CONFUSION_OR_NONE
forbiddenPatterns.description: Accepting algorithm 'none' or symmetric 'HS256' when verifying IdP RS256 JWTs.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Pin algorithm strictly to RS256 in offline JWT verification options.

forbiddenPatterns.name: AUDIENCE_VALIDATION_BYPASS
forbiddenPatterns.description: Omitting audience validation or treating audience mismatch as a warning.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Strictly verify that token 'aud' matches the consumer application's registered CLIENT_ID.

forbiddenPatterns.name: DYNAMIC_REDIRECT_HOST_INJECTION
forbiddenPatterns.description: Constructing redirect_uri dynamically using the incoming request Host header or untrusted query parameters.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Use explicit, statically configured redirect_uri matching the IdP client registration.

forbiddenPatterns.name: OPEN_REDIRECT_RETURN_TO
forbiddenPatterns.description: Permitting post-login returnTo destinations pointing to external URLs (https://evil.com or //evil.com).
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Validate that returnTo is a relative path starting with '/' and not '//'.

forbiddenPatterns.name: GLOBAL_CORS_WILDCARD
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Configure CORS origins strictly per registered client policy; do not conflate CORS origin with redirect URI.

forbiddenPatterns.name: ENV_BASED_AUTH_BYPASS
forbiddenPatterns.description: Bypassing authentication or token checks when NODE_ENV !== 'production'.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Enforce authentication unconditionally; use mock providers or test harnesses in tests instead of code bypasses.

forbiddenPatterns.name: DISABLE_AUTH_FLAG
forbiddenPatterns.description: Introducing DISABLE_AUTH or SKIP_AUTH flags into application logic or production configuration.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Remove all authentication bypass flags; security controls must remain intact across all environments.

forbiddenPatterns.name: CONFLATING_ISDEV_WITH_ISPUBLIC
forbiddenPatterns.description: Treating isDev as isPublic or assuming development clients are public SPAs.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: isDev controls loopback URI permission; isPublic controls whether client possesses a secret or has open tenant access.

forbiddenPatterns.name: CONFLATING_AUTHN_WITH_AUTHZ
forbiddenPatterns.description: Treating successful IdP authentication as application authorization or administrator access.
forbiddenPatterns.remediation: Implement consumer-level business authorization checks independently of IdP identity.

securityReviewQuestions: 1. Is the client public or confidential?
2. Is this client development or production?
3. Is the callback URI exactly registered?
5. Is localhost used only for explicitly configured development?
14. Is application authorization separate from authentication?
17. Is there a development bypass that can activate in production?
18. Are production and development configuration isolated?
